title: claude-autoresume config.json
description: User settings at ~/.claude-autoresume/config.json: account type, dollar budgets, remote SSH hosts, and Sessions-list retention. On the Mac the widget's Settings window is the ONLY writer (read-modify-write under config.json.lock, tmp + replaceItemAt, unknown keys preserved); the Python side only ever reads, defensively, treating a missing or malformed file as the full default config. On a REMOTE host remote_ctl.py apply-config may additionally write - solely as a relay of the widget's sessions.idle_retention_minutes, same lock and atomic-write discipline, never touching any other key. The daemon itself never writes this file on any host. Because the sole writer only writes keys the user has actually touched, a real config.json is typically PARTIAL: every block below is optional and every reader must default it.
x-in-band-version-note: This is the only one of the five formats with an in-band `version`. ConfigStore.mutate stamps version=1 on every write if absent. Nothing on either side actually gates behaviour on it yet - see the findings in README.md.
x-writers: ClaudeUsageOverlay ConfigStore (Settings window) - sole writer on the Mac
claude-autoresume/remote_ctl.py apply-config - remote hosts only, sessions.idle_retention_minutes only
x-additional-properties-note: Deliberately open. Unknown-key preservation is a stated design rule: hand-editing must keep working, and ConfigStore's read-modify-write round-trips keys it does not understand.

version.description: Schema version. Written by ConfigStore on every mutation. Read by the widget into AppConfig.version and then unused; never read by Python at all.

account.description: Which billing arrangement the user is on. Drives whether the widget shows Max percentage bars or dollar budget bars, and which tier plan_fit rescales the observed utilization series from.

type.description: 'max' = subscription (percentage bars). 'api' = metered API billing, which swaps the Max % bars for dollar budget bars fed from the plan_fit cost pipeline. Python falls back to 'max' for anything else.
type.x-reader: The Swift decoder does NOT validate against this enum - it copies any string through. See findings F2-2.

plan.description: Canonical plan key. Mirrors plan_fit.TIER_MULTIPLIERS' key set, duplicated in autoresume_config.VALID_PLANS on purpose (that module must not import plan_fit - it is deployed standalone to remote hosts). Anything non-canonical degrades to 'max_20x' AND sets load_config_with_meta's plan_from_file=False, so plan_fit does not record a transient config glitch as a real plan change (which would permanently truncate utilization history). Still used on 'api' accounts, for the tier-comparison ratio.
plan.x-reader: The Swift decoder does NOT validate against this enum. See findings F2-2.

budget.description: Dollar limits per calendar period. Null limit = that bar is not shown. Stored as JSON null rather than 0 so the daemon can distinguish 'unconfigured' from 'zero'.

weekly_usd.description: Weekly dollar budget, or null for none. Python's _positive_number rejects non-finite, non-positive, and boolean values (a bool is not a number here) back to null. The widget rounds to cents on both write and read, so the displayed text round-trips to the stored value.

monthly_usd.description: Monthly dollar budget, or null for none. Same validation as weekly_usd.

week_start.description: Which weekday starts the weekly BUDGET period. Deliberately NOT the Max plan's rolling-7d window - this is a calendar week for spend accounting only.

timezone.description: Which timezone's midnight bounds a budget period. 'local' is DST-safe (each boundary is localized on its own date). NOTE: no code in this repo writes this key - ConfigStore explicitly never touches it - yet both readers consume it. See findings F2-5.

projection_basis.description: Which elapsed clock the budget spend projection extrapolates on. 'calendar' (default) counts every hour of the period. 'weekdays' counts only Mon-Fri hours, on BOTH sides of the spent/elapsed-fraction ratio, so a weekday-only worker is not projected as if the weekend were going to carry spend; weekend spend still counts toward spent_usd, it is just extrapolated over the remaining weekday time. Weekday-ness is judged in the same timezone as the period bounds. Applies to both the weekly and monthly windows.

idle_retention_minutes.description: How long an idle (never-rate-limited) session stays in the Sessions list before the daemon drops its state.json entry. Default 30, matching the historical hardcoded ACTIVE_WINDOW_MINUTES. BOTH sides clamp to 5-1440 on read, so an out-of-range hand-edit displays as what actually takes effect. This is also the one key the Mac relays to enabled remote hosts (one-way by design: the Mac always wins while the host is enabled).

remote_hosts.description: Shape-C remote SSH hosts. The same stdlib daemon runs on each; remote_sync.py on the Mac merges their state in over ssh. Absent entirely when no host has ever been added.

remoteHost.description: One remote host. Python's _clean_host DROPS any entry failing its checks (non-dict, blank/duplicate name, name containing ':', blank ssh) rather than raising; the Swift decoder keeps anything with a name and an ssh string. See findings F2-3.

name.description: Unique host label. May NOT contain ':' because it is the state.json key prefix '<name>::<sid>'. Duplicates are dropped by Python (first wins).

ssh.description: 'user@host' or a ~/.ssh/config alias. Whitespace-trimmed by Python.

enabled.description: Whether the Mac syncs this host. DEFAULT MISMATCH: Python defaults a missing key to TRUE, the Swift decoder to FALSE. See findings F2-1.

python.description: Interpreter to invoke on the remote. Defaults to 'python3' on both sides. Remote boxes only ever get system python3 - the payload is hard-constrained to stdlib.

state_dir.description: The remote's own state directory. Defaults to '~/.claude-autoresume' on both sides.

poll_seconds.description: Sync cadence for this host. Python coerces to int and replaces anything below MIN_HOST_POLL_SECONDS (10) with the default 30; the Swift decoder takes the value verbatim (default 30).

collect_usage.description: Whether the hourly usage lane also pulls this host's token store into usage/remote/<host>_tokens_hourly.json, folding its cost in as a 'code_cli@<host>' surface. Defaults true on both sides.

deployed_at.description: ISO8601 timestamp stamped by HostDeployer on a successful '@@OK' deploy. Informational only. Python coerces a non-string to null.

deployed_version.description: Payload version stamped alongside deployed_at. Informational only. Python coerces a non-string to null.
